title: Agent-assisted consensus design lowers emulated-network latency
summary: A human-supervised coding agent designed A-greement. In six emulated network configurations, mean latency improved by 12.2% for write-heavy and 33.3% for read-heavy workloads relative to the fastest baseline. Authors report Lean-checked linearizability of the encoded protocol, not a proof of every implementation behavior.
ai_technology: GPT-6.1 Sol High in the AI-greement Codex harness

evidence.tested: Implemented key-value workloads on a CPU cluster with emulated network conditions; twelve configurations, with headline averages restricted to six five/nine-replica configurations.
evidence.unknown: Human experts removed benchmark shortcuts and corrected inherited flaws. Write-heavy p99 latency was worse despite lower mean latency. Model safety does not establish implementation equivalence; no independent proof reproduction. Crash-only, non-restarting replicas, majority availability, partial synchrony and bounded clock drift constrain the guarantees.
evidence.ai_role: The agent proposed protocol mechanisms, implemented candidates and constructed Lean specifications/proofs; humans supplied criteria and reviewed designs.

source_review.scope: Primary model, agent-role, verification and evaluation sections; current v1 metadata. Vulnerability counterexamples excluded from review scope.
